title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered 82 of Exposé IX, from Grothendieck's 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie' (SGA 7 I, Exp. IX), §7, 'partie abélienne'. It is filed among handwritten notes on divided-power de Rham complexes and derived functors. The neighbouring pages are unrelated, so this is evidently a stray typescript sheet reused or misfiled.

Setting: V is a complete discrete valuation ring and S = Spec V is a trait. A is a smooth commutative S-group scheme whose special fibre has identity component an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. The main case is A = the Néron model of an abelian variety A_K with semi-stable reduction. Put S_n = Spec V/m^{n+1} and A_n = A ×_S S_n.

Construction:
1. Let T_0 be the maximal torus of A_0, so B_0 = A_0^0/T_0 is an abelian variety.
2. Tori lift uniquely through infinitesimal thickenings (§5.1, after SGA 3 IX). This gives compatible subtori T_n ⊂ A_n^0, that is, a formal subtorus T̂ ⊂ Â.
3. The fppf quotient B_n = A_n^0/T_n is representable (SGA 3 VI_A 3.2). It is flat and of finite type over S_n, with special fibre B_0.
4. Hence B_n is an abelian scheme over S_n: smoothness follows from flatness plus a smooth fibre, and properness can be checked on the reduced fibre. The B_n are compatible under base change, so they form a formal abelian scheme B̂ = (B_n).
5. Grothendieck then announces conditions under which B̂ is algebraizable (EGA III 5.4.1), i.e. is the completion of a projective abelian scheme B over S. B is unique up to unique isomorphism, and the group law algebraizes by full faithfulness of formal completion. This B is called the 'abelian part' A^ab of A.

Purpose: to set up the decomposition of the formal Néron model into toric and abelian parts. This feeds the later description of the semi-stable degeneration and of the monodromy filtration on the Tate module.
errors: Minor wording: A_K is called 'un schéma abélien' over K; it is simply an abelian variety. This is harmless.

No genuine gap. The passage from 'flat of finite type with abelian special fibre' to 'abelian scheme over S_n' uses standard facts (fibrewise smoothness criterion; properness is topological over a nilpotent thickening), which are left implicit.
Algebraizability needs an ample line bundle on B̂ (Grothendieck existence theorem). The text correctly defers this to 'conditions' given later.

ideas.what: Lifting the maximal torus of the special fibre to a formal subtorus of the formal completion of the Néron model
ideas.modern_name: Formal torus of a semi-abelian degeneration / rigidity of tori
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, §5 and §7; SGA 3 Exp. IX

ideas.what: Formal abelian scheme B̂ = (A_n^0/T_n) and its algebraization B = A^ab, the 'abelian part' of A
ideas.modern_name: Abelian part of a semi-abelian degeneration (Raynaud extension 0→T→G→B→0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX); later Raynaud, Mumford, Faltings–Chai

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exp. IX text on the abelian part of the Néron model, apparently misfiled among unrelated derived-category notes. Its content is published and credited to Grothendieck. The only curiosity is archival: the sheet's presence in cote 136.
transcription_corrections: The '400' at the bottom is an archival stamp. A pencilled page number '269' appears at the lower left.
In 'A_o^o/T_o' the superscript o denotes the identity component (neutral component).
